newsitem.title: USA: Cash crude deals in U.S. Gulf soften sweet prices.
newsitem.headline: Cash crude deals in U.S. Gulf soften sweet prices.

text.p: Cash crude grades in the U.S. Gulf attracted attention at mostly weaker prices Wednesday afternoon, while outright values ticked higher within a tight trading range.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing moved around 15-20 cents higher at $19.60-70 a barrel, with August WTI/Cushing some 25-30 cents off that mark at $19.35-45 a barrel, traders said.
Grade business accelerated in volume by the time midday came, with sweet differentials punctured by sentiment plenty of crude remained in storage.
"This has become something of a pattern. There is little volume in the morning after expiration (NYMEX), then business picks up in the afternoon," said cash player.
Friday is pipeline scheduling day for August pipeline space, leaving only Thursday for significant activity, traders said.
"Most refiners will wrap everything up on Thursday, with Friday being the start of a summer weekend," said the dealer.
Trades on Tuesday left Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James with only a 5-10 cents premium to August WTI/Cushing, down from premiums of more than 20-23 cents on Monday and early Tuesday.
Other confirmed sales saw West Texas Sour/Midland barrels move at a $1.45 discount, and Eugene Island swamp supply selling $1.28 cheaper than August WTI/Cushing.
Midland/WTI sold between 29-33 cents under the marker, traders said, steady from previous morning talk.
